gaps: SOUTH AFRICA — TOSAC (The Official South African Charts, RiSA) — COULD NOT READ. NOT A ZERO. theofficialsacharts.co.za/robots.txt names Claude's crawlers explicitly and forbids them: the block listing 'User-Agent: ClaudeBot', 'User-Agent: Claude-User' and 'User-Agent: Claude-SearchBot' (alongside GPTBot, CCBot, PerplexityBot and ~45 others) carries 'Disallow: /' and 'DisallowAITraining: /', and the catch-all 'User-Agent: *' block carries 'Content-Usage: ai=n'. The site enforces this with an anti-crawler tarpit rather than a 403: every path I requested returned HTTP 200 carrying machine-generated filler prose (mashed-up Shakespeare/Othello text) under a title of the form '<title>ai/<requested-path>/</title>' — e.g. /charts/, /about/, /wp-json/wp/v2/posts and /sitemap_index.xml's siblings all returned that maze. In the browser the same paths returned HTTP 421. I did NOT spoof a non-Claude user agent, and did not otherwise attempt to evade the block, so no TOSAC singles or albums peak for either artist was read. This is a hard gap.

NIGERIA — pre-chart era is out of reach by construction, not by failure. Nigeria's principal singles chart begins with its first issue, week of 2020-11-05; the principal albums chart begins 2022-11-02. Olamide's career began in 2011, so his entire pre-November-2020 catalogue (e.g. 'Science Student', 'Wo!!', 'Motigbana', 'Woske', 'Shakiti Bobo', 'Who You Epp') has no Nigerian chart peak that can exist, and his 2020 and 2021 albums 'Carpe Diem' and 'UY Scuti' entered the albums chart only after it launched, so their recorded peaks (33 and 84) are peaks-within-the-chart's-lifetime, not all-time peaks. This limits what the 103 figure means; it is not an unread chart.

GHANA — resolved as 'no national chart exists' rather than left as a gap, but one residual uncertainty is recorded honestly: ghamro.org resolves to 54.88.98.248 yet never completes a TCP connection on either scheme, and musiga.org.gh has no DNS record at all, so neither Ghanaian body's own site could be read directly this pass. Neither organisation is a chart compiler (GHAMRO is a royalty collection society, MUSIGA a musicians' union) and no other evidence of a Ghanaian national chart was found, so this does not change the conclusion — but if a Ghanaian chart programme were ever announced only on those two hosts, I would not have seen it.
